pages.text: Spring had come. Yuki stepped into the yard with a basket. Momo hopped ahead.
"I'll bring mugwort. Please make mugwort rice cakes." Grandma nodded.
Pointed mugwort shoots grew on the slope where snow had melted. Yuki picked them into the basket. It filled quickly.
Bigger shoots stood over there. "Just one more." Yuki picked those, too, piling them on top.
No more would fit. Yuki hugged the extra mugwort. Both hands were full.
The path down was slippery. Yuki's foot slid.
The mugwort spilled into the mud. Picking it up, Yuki found it covered in dirt. "We can't eat this."
Grandma opened Yuki's hands. "You only have two hands."
The next day, Yuki filled just half the basket. "I'll pick the rest tomorrow." Both hands felt light.
At the bottom of the slope, Yuki offered the basket. Grandma shaped soft green dough with her hands.
